minutes.headline: Commission denied a certificate of compliance at 564 Page Street over unestablished plantings; approved a trial snow groomer on trails.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission met by Zoom and heard a resident's field-change request it could not act on because it was unposted. It approved a temporary allowance for a Snow Dog trail groomer, approved several permits and certificates of compliance, and denied one certificate over unestablished plantings. It also voted to send a second violation notice with a daily fine, and deferred a fine decision on a Fire Road enforcement case to December 4.

budget_items.what_was_said: The administrator said a second notice, per town counsel's guidance, would include a daily fine. The commission voted to cite it if the application is not completed by December 4.

The administrator read from the enforcement order that civil penalties could reach a stated maximum for each violation, with each day a separate offense. The commission deferred a decision on fines to December 4.
The chair said the snowmobile club had set aside a capped sum for banners marking official trail work on its power units.
Members discussed whether rent from the caretaker residence must go back into the Hollis account. The lease says it does, but an advisor found no deed or conservation restriction requiring it.

budget_items.topic: Cabinets for the Hollis Road residence kitchen
budget_items.what_was_said: The cabinets were bought by someone else before the volunteer could buy them. Funds were already authorized for the purchase.
The snow riders received an ATV power unit paid for under a commission-sponsored grant, and are working on registration. The grant terms require a Mass Trails plaque on it.

decisions.decision: Commission agreed in principle to pursue a permanent trail-use regulation change covering snow groomers, with generic language not tied to a brand. It will take it up later so absent members can weigh in, and the required televised hearings cannot happen yet.
The applicant at 564 Page Street was invited to reapply in the spring once vegetation has leafed out.
The administrator will tell the Fire Road respondent that the appeal route is no longer available. She will meet town counsel on the fine process, and the commission will take up fines on December 4.
205 Sunset will come off the enforcement list because town counsel advised the commission lost authority once DEP issued a superseding order of conditions.
The Island Road owners should file a retroactive request for determination within 30 days.
Next meeting is December 4; there will be no meeting on the 20th because the administrator is out.
Members were open to a work-notice plaque or banner on the trail ATV when the commission has approved work; Chris will look into making it.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission denied a certificate of compliance at 564 Page Street, and the applicant was invited to reapply in the spring once vegetation has leafed out.
The commission voted a temporary deviation from its regulations to allow a Snow Dog trail groomer on conservation trails, and agreed in principle to pursue a permanent rule.
It voted to issue a second violation notice at 10 Massachusetts Ave, with a daily fine if the application is not completed by December 4.
A decision on fines in the Fire Road enforcement case was deferred to December 4, pending a meeting between the administrator and town counsel.
The commission approved a notice of intent at 701 Reservoir Road and certificates of compliance at 48 Pearl Street and 393 New West Townsend Road.

why_it_matters: Certificates of compliance close out permitted work on a property, so a denial over unestablished plantings keeps that file open until the vegetation is judged established.
The groomer allowance is temporary and a permanent trail-use regulation has not been written, so who may use conservation trails and with what equipment remains open to change.
Whether daily fines are imposed in the two enforcement cases will be settled at the December 4 meeting, after the administrator consults town counsel on the fine process.
watch_next: December 4 meeting: the Fire Road fine decision, the 10 Massachusetts Ave application deadline, and the continued DNA Lunenburg and 390 Howard Street filings.
A permanent trail-use regulation for snow groomers, which the commission said it will take up later so absent members can weigh in.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on nearly every vote, but they disagree on who was present for the DNA/D & A Lunenburg continuance: the official minutes show Jeff voting aye (5-0), while ours has Jeff absent and four votes. The official minutes also leave out several items from the recording (the permanent groomer regulation, the 205 Sunset removal, the ATV banner idea, the $25,000 Fire Road penalty) and add some items ours lacks (Hollis Road, 586 Reservoir Road, the 390 Howard site visit).
